Design mock review index
Overnight refinement pass, 2026-08-21/22 — every screen mocked as standalone HTML importing the real hub/ui/src/index.css tokens, in both themes, screenshotted and read (not just rendered) before being called done. Built incrementally, one entry per screen as its four passes finish — see .claude/autonomous/2026-08-21-refine-and-continue-log.md for the full trail. Screenshots below are inlined as data-URIs, not committed as .png files — the repo's blanket *.png .gitignore rule blocks that.
S1 — Conversation + composer + left navigation
4/4 passes done
The main screen — ConversationView, AgentTimeline (MessageEntry, WorkRow, OutboundMessageEntry), the composer and its control row, and Sidebar/AgentTree/SidebarItem. Six verified gaps from RESEARCH.md — no message copy affordance, a wired-but-invisible composer "armed" state, one dimmed send-button look for two different waits, a bare context-usage bar, timestamps with no path to precision, and pre-U0a motion — fixed in two variants exploring degree (restrained / considered), never a different design language. Full writeup in RATIONALE.md, including two judgement calls made by looking at the actual render: a pinned-open popover overlap deliberately left as-is (standard transient hover behaviour), and a real last-message clipping bug caused by the mocks never scrolling their timeline to the newest entry the way the live app's AgentOutputPanel.tsx always does — found and fixed this pass.

Before / after — a real bug found by looking, not by reading source
Neither mock scrolled its .timeline to the newest entry on load. The live product always does (AgentOutputPanel.tsx: scrollTop = scrollHeight in the simple case, specifically so a conversation shows its newest message regardless of window focus). Without it, the static frame's own overflow boundary cut the last message off mid-line, right where the composer begins. Fixed by scrolling every .timeline to scrollHeight on load, in both variants.
before — clipped mid-line
after — full message + working indicator visible
S2 — Task board + task cards
4/4 passes done
The operator named this screen the worst offender, verbatim: “The cards look very plain, with no texture, no animation or fine details just a box with things written on it and the task board the same.” TasksBoard, TaskCard, TaskDetailDrawer, TaskIntegrationNote. Ten verified gaps from RESEARCH.md — including a real product bug where every task priority renders an identical grey pill — fixed in two variants (restrained / considered). Two further bugs found beyond RESEARCH.md itself: a present-tense icon-mapping bug already live in the shipped product (four Icon names used that don’t exist in Icon.tsx’s map, rendering nothing), and a flag-glyph legibility bug in the mock’s own priority badge, caught by screenshotting and reading, not from the source — see the before/after below. Full writeup, including why the restrained variant’s plain colour dot turned out to be the structurally safer choice at this information density, in RATIONALE.md.

Before / after — a legibility bug found by looking, not by reading source
The FLAG/FLAG_SM glyph built to disambiguate high/critical priority by shape was a thin stroke-width: 2.4 outline at 9px — rendered, it read as the letter “P,” not a flag, in both themes, at every call site. Comparing against the card’s other small glyphs (a thin-stroke warning triangle at 11px reads fine) isolated the cause as the flag’s own geometry, not size alone. Fixed by rebuilding it as a filled shape and bumping both call sites from 9px to 11px.
before — reads as “P,” not a flag
after — filled shape, 11px, legible in both themes
